lines: Intermittent right upper quadrant discomfort after meals with bloating

encounters.cc: Right heel pain for two months, worse with first steps in the morning

lines: Right heel pain for two months, worse with first steps in the morning
This 47-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, hypothyroidism, and chronic constipation, recently evaluated for cholelithiasis, presents with two-month history of right heel pain.
She states the pain is most noticeable when she first gets out of bed in the morning.
It feels like a sharp pulling sensation along the bottom of her heel, which sometimes radiates forward along the arch of her foot.
After walking for a few minutes, the pain lessens, and she is generally able to go about her day with only mild discomfort.
However, the pain often returns if she has been sitting or inactive for long periods and then stands up again.
She has not had any recent trauma or systemic symptoms.
- No prior abdominal or pelvic surgery
- Ibuprofen 200-400 mg PO every 6-8 hours as needed for pain
She works in retail and spends most of her day standing or walking on hard floors.
On physical examination, there is point tenderness at the medial calcaneal tuberosity of the right foot.
There is no swelling, erythema, or warmth.

encounters.cc: Progressively worsening pain at the bottom of her right foot over the past 3 months

lines: Progressively worsening pain at the bottom of her right foot over the past 3 months
This patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, and hypothyroidism returns for follow-up of right foot pain previously evaluated.
She reports that the pain is most severe when she takes her first steps in the morning or after sitting for long periods.
She works as a teacher and is on her feet most of the day, which exacerbates her discomfort.
- No prior abdominal or pelvic surgery
- Ibuprofen 200-400 mg PO every 6-8 hours as needed for pain
Occupation: Elementary school teacher; previously employed in retail sales.
There is tenderness to palpation at the anterior aspect of the calcaneus, and the pain is reproduced with passive dorsiflexion of her toes.
An X-ray of the foot is obtained and reveals a small calcaneal spur.

encounters.cc: Three-month history of right heel pain unresponsive to OTC medications

lines: Three-month history of right heel pain unresponsive to OTC medications
This 47-year-old female with Type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, and hypothyroidism returns for follow-up evaluation of right heel pain previously assessed in March and April 2020.
She reports a 3-month history of right heel pain worse in the morning and after periods of rest, improving slightly after walking a few minutes but worsening with prolonged standing.
She has tried over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen with minimal relief.
- No prior abdominal or pelvic surgery
- Ibuprofen 200-400 mg PO every 6-8 hours as needed for pain
Occupation: Elementary school teacher; previously employed in retail sales.
Tenderness to palpation at the anteromedial aspect of the right calcaneus.
Passive dorsiflexion of the toes elicits pain in the heel.
Ankle dorsiflexion and plantar flexion are within normal limits.
Radiographs of the foot show a calcaneal spur.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of urinary incontinence with urgency and leakage

lines: Six-month history of urinary incontinence with urgency and leakage

This 48-year-old patient with Type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, hypothyroidism, and chronic constipation, previously evaluated for cholelithiasis and plantar fasciitis, presents to the obstetrics and gynecology clinic.
She reports that she experiences urine leakage with coughing and sneezing, as well as a sudden, overwhelming urge to urinate that she cannot always control.
She has had several episodes of incontinence on the way to the bathroom.
Her past medical history includes type 2 diabetes mellitus, well-controlled on metformin, and two vaginal deliveries.
- No prior abdominal or pelvic surgery
Her medications include metformin and a daily multivitamin.
- Ibuprofen 200-400 mg PO every 6-8 hours as needed for pain
Occupation: Elementary school teacher; previously employed in retail sales.
She denies any hematuria, dysuria, or nocturia.
On physical examination, her BMI is 31 kg/m^2, and there is no suprapubic tenderness or masses.
A cough stress test provokes a small amount of urine leakage.
Urinalysis is negative for infection or hematuria.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of a bulging sensation in the perineum during defecation

lines: Six-month history of a bulging sensation in the perineum during defecation

The patient is a 48-year-old female with chronic constipation and prior evaluation for urinary incontinence six months ago who presents with a six-month history of a sensation of a bulge in her perineum, which she notices most prominently while defecating.
She reports that the bulge occasionally protrudes through her anal canal, especially after prolonged standing or coughing.
She has a history of chronic constipation and has given birth vaginally to three children.
- No prior abdominal or pelvic surgery
- Ibuprofen 200-400 mg PO every 6-8 hours as needed for pain
Occupation: Elementary school teacher; previously employed in retail sales.
On physical examination, a soft, red, doughnut-shaped mass is visible at the anal verge during Valsalva maneuver, which reduces spontaneously when she lies down.
Rectal examination confirms the presence of a full-thickness rectal prolapse.

encounters.cc: Worsening perianal bulge requiring manual reduction with mucous discharge

lines: Worsening perianal bulge requiring manual reduction with mucous discharge
The patient is a 48-year-old female with chronic constipation and obesity who returns with worsening symptoms following her evaluation two months ago.
She reports a 6-month history of a sensation of a bulge in her perianal area noticed especially during defecation.
The bulge sometimes reduces spontaneously, but she must manually push it back in at other times.
She also complains of occasional mucous discharge and a recent onset of fecal incontinence.
- Ibuprofen 200-400 mg PO every 6-8 hours as needed for pain
Occupation: Elementary school teacher; previously employed in retail sales.
On physical examination, you observe a reddish, doughnut-shaped mass with concentric rings protruding from the anal orifice when she strains.
The mass reduces when she stops straining.
Rectal examination reveals decreased anal sphincter tone.

lines: Two-month history of pruritus, pale stools, and dark urine with RUQ fullness
The patient with cholelithiasis diagnosed in 2020 presents with recurrent right upper quadrant symptoms.
She denies any significant pain but reports a feeling of fullness in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen.

- No prior abdominal or pelvic surgery
- Ibuprofen 200-400 mg PO every 6-8 hours as needed for pain
On physical examination, her skin and sclera are icteric.
Her abdomen is soft, non-tender, with no palpable masses, but there is mild hepatomegaly.
